stories.situation: Triangle spikes the morning cider with pickle juice and booby-traps his own haunted cave, and the jam his friends spent all morning making becomes the punchline. Circle and Square walk out of Halloween entirely and start a rival holiday of pure treats, while the king of Halloween is left alone in the dark, going deeper to find his way out.
stories.coping: Square and Circle say the line plainly, the trick went too far, and let the silence do the talking. When the prank master himself gets lost and lonely enough to sing about missing his friends, the apology is his own idea, and the treat party, the cave creatures, and the costume chest all end up under one roof.
stories.notes: single-story episode, no segment in catalog. mixed age: cave gags and the costume chest play 2-4; a prank that lands as unkind, and how the pranker repairs it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'all treats and no tricks' skips the cave snail Susan, the mimic monsters, and that Triangle's apology names what he was wrong about specifically. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: After Triangle pranks them, Circle and Square celebrate Halloween on their own with all treats and no tricks.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Halloween starts with pickle juice in the cider mug and ends with Circle and Square declaring a rival all-treats holiday after Triangle's haunted cave burns their homemade jam as a prank. Deep in the cave, the self-crowned king of Halloween gets exactly what his tricks deserve, lost, alone, and singing Halloween carols to cave creatures who hold him like a subject. The friends who were too mad to speak miss him too, and the apology he rehearses into the dark is the trick that finally brings everyone, monsters included, to a costume party.

stories.episodeTitle: Narrator's Big Day / Square's Time Chest
stories.situation: Nothing is happening on The Island, and the Narrator's job is to observe and tell, never to change or affect the story. She confesses how hard that is, how she wishes she could make her own stories instead of waiting for one to show up, right before a beetle egg hatches into the little grub she names Sarah.
stories.coping: Watching Sarah crawl, nearly freeze, and nearly become a bird's lunch pushes the Narrator past the rule that narrators stay out of it: she speaks up, tells the bird to drop that bug, and it does. She saves the story herself and finds a voice she did not know she had.
stories.notes: mixed age: the egg-to-beetle bug saga plays 2-4; the meta idea of a narrator who is only supposed to watch, and the choice to break a rule to help, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'gives Narrator time to herself' hides that the whole story is the beetle's one-day metamorphosis and that the Narrator intervenes. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The Shapes' rather ordinary day gives Narrator time to herself. Square struggles to find the perfect object for the island's new time capsule.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The Island has nothing going on, and the Narrator, whose whole job is to wait for stories, admits how lonely that can feel. Then a leaf hides a Drabling Beetle egg, and she pours herself into the little grub she names Sarah: first meal, harrowing pinecone, cocoon surprise, and one very hungry bird. A narrator is not supposed to change the story, but she talks the bird into dropping Sarah anyway, and the voice she found stays with her long after the beetle flies off.

stories.episodeTitle: Narrator's Big Day / Square's Time Chest
stories.situation: Triangle invents the time chest, a box of treasure buried for future generations, and Square freezes: what object represents who he is? Nothing in his house qualifies, and his answer, the biggest block in the cave, is a treasure the size of a lifestyle, which the three friends attempt to pull out of the ground anyway.
stories.coping: Square says out loud that he has no genius plans like his friends, only one dumb plan of his own, and it is the one that works. When the runaway block buries them all, the laughter decides it: he leaves the book instead, and the three pull it back out of the hole together.
stories.notes: mixed age: heave-ho treasure comedy plays 2-4; what it means to leave something of yourself behind, and that your quiet everyday thing is enough, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'struggles to find the perfect object' skips the block extraction saga, the baby blanket friction trick, and the ending choice of the book. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The Shapes' rather ordinary day gives Narrator time to herself. Square struggles to find the perfect object for the island's new time capsule.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Triangle buries a chest of treasures for the future, and Square cannot pick a single thing to represent himself. After rejecting candy wrappers and rusty stools, he lands on the biggest block in his cave, and moving it takes every plan his friends have plus the one he thought was dumb. The block wins, everyone laughs, and Square buries the real answer, a book, the quietest possible evidence of exactly who he is.

stories.situation: Triangle spots Square's rare Lightning Chicken card and offers the glitter pen, the gift Circle just gave him, in trade. He says yes before he thinks, and one imagined heart-shattering speech later, Square is planning his own exile to the far side of the island rather than tell her what he did.
stories.coping: Square decides it will only get harder and comes clean, braced for the worst punishment he can imagine, self-banishment included. Circle's answer reframes everything: it was a pen, and he is still her friend, the kind who overthinks and worries a bit too much.
stories.notes: mixed age: the trade comedy plays 2-4; guilt loud enough to invent a Shame voice, and the discovery that the truth is smaller than the dread, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'feels guilty after trading away a gift' is the spine; the script adds the Shame-banishment spiral and Circle's generous shrug. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Square feels guilty after trading away a gift from Circle. Square and Circle try to find the source of Triangle's allergy.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Square trades the glitter pen Circle gave him for the last card his collection will ever need, and the guilt arrives before the card does. A figment named Shame narrates his night: her heart will shatter, banishment is the only decent response, the bags are already packed. When he finally confesses, ready for exile, Circle cannot even remember which pen, and the whole weight of the betrayal turns out to weigh almost nothing to the friend who gave it.

stories.situation: Triangle is sneezing and miserable, and his friends mount an all-out allergy hunt: eliminate everything, hazmat suits, trash-watching, garden raids. The mystery is really about them, since Triangle has known the answer all along and has been protecting it, and his secrets look so strange from outside that Square briefly diagnoses a Were-Sloth.
stories.coping: Triangle finally says what he knew the whole time, animal dander, and why he hid it: eliminating the source forever would mean eliminating his furry friends. The friends admit they jumped to conclusions, and the cure becomes visiting the animals together.
stories.notes: mixed age: hazmat suits and sneezes play 2-4; help that will not listen, and friends who jump to unfair conclusions about what they do not understand, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'try to find the source of Triangle's allergy' hides the Were-Sloth panic, the garbage archaeology, and that Triangle shielded his animal friends on purpose. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Square feels guilty after trading away a gift from Circle. Square and Circle try to find the source of Triangle's allergy.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Triangle's allergies set off the most thorough friend investigation on The Island: one item at a time reintroduction, a birder stakeout, an ascent through garbage, skunk cabbage, and stolen worms. The stranger they keep finding looks less and less like their Triangle, and Square lands on a monster explanation before the truth surfaces: Triangle knew it was animal dander from the start and said nothing, because his friends kept promising to eliminate the source forever, and the source is his best friends.

stories.episodeTitle: Square's Missing Mug / Triangle Stands Still
stories.situation: Square's favorite mug vanishes on the same morning he woke up already upset, and the case of the mugnapping uncovers everything but the mug: a shell he cannot stop returning to, a quad rainbow, and a picnic toast nobody noticed. The real mystery is why he was upset before the mug went missing.
stories.coping: Under gentle pressure from two detectives who genuinely want to help, Square admits the thing he called silly: the toast he never got to give, and the times his friends walked away mid-moment. They apologize, and when Turtle the bloodhound locates the mug, the postponed toast finally happens.
stories.notes: mixed age: the mugnapping investigation plays 2-4; the buried hurt underneath a small crisis, and finding the courage to say the silly feeling out loud, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'island-wide hunt' skips that the clue trail is really Square's own unspoken feelings, and that the mug was in the picnic basket all along. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The disappearance of Square's favorite mug sends him on an island-wide hunt. Triangle bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still for ten minutes.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The morning starts with a missing mug and ends with a solved friendship. Square, Circle, and Triangle run a full detective operation, turtle scent lines, grasshopper print forensics, an inside-job accusation, while the actual evidence keeps pointing somewhere none of them want to look: the picnic where Square tried to toast his gratitude and both friends wandered off after a rainbow. When he finally names the hurt he had been carrying since before the mug vanished, the case cracks open, Turtle finds the mug, and the toast lands.

stories.episodeTitle: Square's Missing Mug / Triangle Stands Still
stories.situation: Triangle claims doing nothing is the easiest thing there is, and one boast later he is locked into a bet: stand still for ten minutes. An itch, a marching column of ants, and his own buzzing mind all conspire, and stillness turns out to be the hardest thing he has ever done.
stories.coping: Circle coaches instead of rescuing: acknowledge the itch, acknowledge the ants, return to the breath. Triangle follows his breathing all the way into hearing colors, then steps out with one second left and hands the bet back, the tranquility already worth more than winning.
stories.notes: mixed age: ants and the itch acknowledgment play 2-4; the felt difference between sitting still and actually being present, lands 5-7 too. script_vs_synopsis: 'bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still' is right; the script adds the internal visit from his own itch and the last-second forfeit that shows he meditated for the feeling, not the prize. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The disappearance of Square's favorite mug sends him on an island-wide hunt. Triangle bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still for ten minutes.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Triangle is the calmest person he knows, he dares anyone to say otherwise, and the dare becomes a ten-minute stillness bet he almost immediately regrets. Circle walks him through the real thing, acknowledge the itch, greet the ants climbing his shape, return to the breath, until the fidgety triangle drifts into a quiet deep enough to hear colors. He steps out at nine minutes fifty-nine, losing the bet on purpose and keeping the peace.

stories.situation: Circle's cave floods overnight and the only bed available is Triangle's, whose world is loud music, handle-bowls, and stains that add character. She adapts to the Triangle Way a little too well, loud music, soaking bowls, shallow uninspired art, until her host realizes there is room for only one Triangle in that house.
stories.coping: Both friends bend honestly toward each other before either admits the cost: Circle misses her plants, her books, her waterfall, and Triangle says the hard sentence kindly, get out of my house. The going home is the resolution, and Circle adds handles to her own bowls instead of her own habits.
stories.notes: mixed age: the flood and the messy sleepover play 2-4; becoming someone else to fit in, and the friend who loves you enough to send you home, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'suddenly needs a place to stay' hides the overcorrection arc, Triangle's mirror complaint, and the mutual lesson. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Circle wakes up to a surprise and suddenly needs a place to stay. A new visitor to the island creates quite a stir.
stories.perStorySynopsis: A flooded cave sends tidy Circle to Casa de Triangle, where dinner is surprise soup, art is a book about triangle high fives, and dishes soak on principle. She loosens up so completely that she stops rinsing, turns the music up, and starts talking about staying for years, while her host privately mourns his system. The rescue is honest in both directions: Triangle tells her to go home because their friendship can hold it, and Circle returns to her own cave grateful, keeping one Triangle Way upgrade, bowls with handles.

stories.situation: A little frog washes ashore and all three shapes want to adopt it, so they stage a contest: one day each to give the frog the best time, then the frog chooses. Culture day, structure day, and a full froggy carnival follow, none of it the frog's idea.
stories.coping: Losing to a ratty old bucket cracks the contest open: they showed the frog everything they liked and never asked it anything. The new plan is friendship without ownership, visits anytime, and the bucket stays exactly where the frog put it.
stories.notes: mixed age: the carnival day plays 2-4; wanting something so much you forget to ask what it wants, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'creates quite a stir' skips the three-day contest structure, the spying, and that the frog chooses an empty bucket over all of them. confidence high.

The frog picks the bucket it rode in on, and the friends get the story's real prize, learning that loving something means asking what it wants, then a new friend on the beach they can visit anytime.

stories.episodeTitle: From Top to Bottom / Circle's Equal
stories.situation: Circle wins every Big-Hill Race without breaking a sweat, mostly because she can float, and Square and Triangle spend each race sabotaging each other instead of racing. This month they try a new strategy: team up, share the cake fifty fifty, and beat her together.
stories.coping: The pact holds where the tricks never did: they pull each other out of trouble, refuse to leave anyone behind, and finish faster than they ever have. They still lose to Circle, and this time there is cake left to split, which tastes like the win it actually is.
stories.notes: mixed age: the obstacle-course slapstick plays 2-4; trading solo losing for teamwork, and keeping the deal when winning alone is one jump away, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'face off in a wild race' hides the sabotage habit, the nobody-gets-left-behind turn, and Circle's offer of a slice afterward. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Circle, Square, and Triangle face off in a wild race for a tasty prize. Circle is thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Big-Hill Race Day ends the same way every month, Circle floating to an easy win while her two rivals trip each other. This time Square and Triangle race as a team, the cake split fifty fifty, and the cooperation pays off in caves, on the rickety bridge, and in the quicksand where Square turns back for a partner instead of a prize. Circle still wins without breaking a sweat, but she leaves them a slice and a new record, and for the first time the losing side feels like winners.

stories.episodeTitle: From Top to Bottom / Circle's Equal
stories.situation: Proto Circle, an older, faster, more magical shape who scans everything, arrives on the island, and everyone falls for her. Circle, who has quietly wished for an equal, starts losing at her own magic, rainbow included, and ends up alone on the roof of her cave feeling replaced.
stories.coping: Proto finds her there and says the true thing, that she comes to this spot when she is upset too, and that there is nothing wrong with having more to learn. Circle says the quiet part out loud, that she felt replaced, and hears back that she is exactly the kind of shape she hoped existed.
stories.notes: mixed age: the scanning robot and the terrarium flourishes play 2-4; the always-most-everything friend meeting someone better, and saying she feels replaced, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her' is the setup, not the arc; the script's middle is envy of a hero and its end is comfort between two solitary elders. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Circle, Square, and Triangle face off in a wild race for a tasty prize. Circle is thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Circle has spent her whole long life as the oldest, wisest, most magical shape on the island, and one day a visitor lands who outdoes all of it. Proto Circle scans everything, knows turtle shell vocabulary, and does circles better than Circle, who tries a flashy rainbow to keep up and meets the roof of her cave instead. The two settle it the way only equals can, by admitting they go to the same lonely spot when they are upset, and Circle sends her off knowing there are others like her out there.

stories.situation: They forgot Circle's Birthday Sunset, an occasion she names out loud right before they promise they did not, and panic sets in. With no gift and no time, a seagrass basket full of oddments turns out to be an ancient treasure map, and the two set off across the island to find something worthy of her before sunset.
stories.coping: They tell Circle the truth before she can pretend it did not happen: we forgot, then spent all day trying to fix it. The empty X at the end turns out to be Circle's own secret spot, and the treasure was never buyable, an omelet recipe she finally has friends to share.
stories.notes: mixed age: the treasure hunt plays 2-4; forgetting something important to a friend, and how showing up with the truth beats showing up with a gift, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure' omits the forgotten Birthday Sunset, the eggs-and-tortoise detours, and that the map is Circle's own recipe. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Triangle and Square follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure. Circle's hat design inspires her to make one hat a day.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Circle mentions tonight's Birthday Sunset, and Square and Triangle realize, mid-bow-wave, that they forgot it completely. Their gift hunt turns a basket of trinkets into an ancient map, and the day becomes a sprint through hens, tortoises, glowing snapdragons, and one very dark cave, all for a final X that holds nothing. Nothing, that is, except Circle's secret rooftop, where the truth earns a bigger welcome than any treasure, and an omelet cooked on sun-warmed rock as the sun goes down.

stories.situation: One flower-on-a-hat earns Circle a standing ovation and turns into a pledge: a brand new hat every day, forever. The ideas thin out fast, and with a fashion show scheduled and her friends expecting the ultimate headliner hat, Circle runs completely out of inspiration.
stories.coping: Circle tells the truth instead of faking it: I burned out, I have nothing, I am sorry. Her friends crown the empty head anyway, hatless and happy beats stressed and spectacular, and their own drained inspiration, straight home and do nothing, is the reviews that matter.
stories.notes: mixed age: the fashion show gags play 2-4; creative burnout, a promise that outgrew itself, and being loved with nothing to show, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'inspires her to make one hat a day' omits the daily drain, the impossible headliner expectations, and the standing ovation for no hat at all. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Triangle and Square follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure. Circle's hat design inspires her to make one hat a day.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Circle's flower-topped hat is such a hit that she promises the island a new design every day, an artist's pledge that becomes a treadmill. By fashion show night, with Square's firefly lightscape and Triangle's stage waiting, she has nothing: the ultimate hat does not exist, and she walks out empty. The avant garde verdicts rain down anyway, because her friends would rather see her hatless and happy than bent over a deadline, and inspiration, it turns out, comes back once you stop chasing it.

stories.episodeTitle: Triangle Has Superpowers / The Sound of Circle
stories.situation: Rain cancels Puzzles by the Sea the morning after Triangle wishes on a leaf that looks like a star, and he decides the wish worked, which means the second wish, superpowers, worked too. The power hunt comes up empty through glow tests, speed sprints, and mind reading, and he cannot bear going back to being just regular old me.
stories.coping: When the trick behind the growing test breaks his heart, his friends tell him the true inventory: he makes them laugh, he is loyal and full of energy, he has a special way with animals. Super Triangle rebrands the canceled puzzle morning instead, umbrella edition, and saves the day his way.
stories.notes: mixed age: the power-testing gags play 2-4; wanting to be special, and learning the special thing is already yours, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'convinced his wish has come true' skips the fake test, the betrayal wobble, and that the friends' answer names his ordinary gifts as the powers. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: After wishing on a star, Triangle is convinced his wish has come true. Triangle and Square want Circle to join their band.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Triangle wishes on a leaf he squints into a star, and when rain cancels puzzle morning he is sure the magic is real, superpowers included. The recovery is better than the wish: his friends list what he actually does, the laughs, the loyalty, the animal whispering, and a canceled puzzle session becomes Puzzles by the Sea Under an Umbrella, saved by Super Triangle.

stories.episodeTitle: Triangle Has Superpowers / The Sound of Circle
stories.situation: Triangle and Square love their band and set about finding Circle a sound that fits it, coaching her through rhythm, melody, and finally the coconut bonker, the one sound she could make without making it weird. Every lesson lands like a correction, and the frog's unanswered song is playing somewhere underneath.
stories.coping: Circle turns the spot down out loud: she was happy to look for a new sound, but in the end it has to sound like her. Alone in her cave that night she plays anyway, and the band realizes their own music is suddenly, inexplicably better with her strange sound underneath it.
stories.notes: mixed age: coconut bonking plays 2-4; being reshaped to fit a group, and choosing your own sound, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'want Circle to join their band' hides the fix-her curriculum, her polite refusal, and the ending where her solo music completes their track from afar. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: After wishing on a star, Triangle is convinced his wish has come true. Triangle and Square want Circle to join their band.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The Whistlesnappers invite Circle to join the band and immediately start fixing her: rhythm from the waves, melody from the lovebirds, and when all that comes out weird, a coconut to bonk. Circle declines with the quietest kind of courage, saying she likes her own sound, and goes home to play for herself. That night the band hears something new under their set and cannot argue with it, because Circle's music, the sound they tried to change, is the part that makes them sound better than ever.

stories.situation: A storm strips the cliff and exposes fossils on a timer: the tide comes back tonight. Then Circle shrinks to a tiny potato of herself, her powers sputtering, and the island's designated helper starts refusing all help while quietly building an elaborate machine to avoid asking for any.
stories.coping: The rock pile collapses and the blame finally cracks her open: helping is supposed to be my job, I am not supposed to need any help. She says the sentence she has never said, I need your help, and with tiny magic in a bucket she solves the tooth herself, with her friends beside her.
stories.notes: mixed age: the dig race plays 2-4; the helper who cannot be helped, and the shame of shrinking while everyone coos Tiny Circle, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'determined to prove she doesn't need help' is the spine; the script adds the beachcomber avoidance machine, the pile collapse, and the accusation scene that ends in the first ask. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: A teeny-tiny Circle is determined to prove she doesn't need help. The Shapes run into obstacles trying to take their yearly picture.
stories.perStorySynopsis: A giant ancient tooth appears in a storm-cut cliff with one tide left to excavate it, and the dig is on, Triangle smashing, Square chipping, Circle hauling. Then a hiccup shrinks her magic and her body, her friends start baby-talking Itsy-Bitsy Circle, and the helper of the island quietly swaps asking for help with building a water-powered scoop machine. The pile collapses, the accusations fly, and it takes the word help, said out loud for the first time, to finish the museum before the sea does.

stories.situation: Picture Day runs on traditions, the same spot, fancy outfits, the choreographed handshake, and Triangle's new shortcut breaks all of them at once: brambles, hair humidity, a tar pool, and a gap that ends the path to the picture spot itself. The camera, it turns out, has been recording the whole disaster.
stories.coping: Circle remembers the tradition the mud did not touch, that the day is about documenting a long-lasting friendship, and declares the party on from inside the mess. The stuck shutter becomes the best archive they own, four seasons of disasters and laughing.
stories.notes: mixed age: the shortcut gauntlet plays 2-4; broken traditions and the discovery that the real tradition is the people in the picture, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'obstacles trying to take their yearly picture' hides that the camera was stuck on all day, so the ruining and the saving are the same reel. confidence high.

The camera's accidental reel of the entire disaster becomes the truest portrait of a long-lasting, beautiful friendship.

stories.situation: Sam's wipeout reveals a glowing underwater cavern and a gold doubloon, and she wants the whole summer adventure to be her and Jade against the mystery. But Jade has science camp and her old camp friends now, and Sam's red-flag surf lands her in trouble with her parents and a confiscated phone while Jade pulls away.
stories.coping: Sam pushes on alone and leaves Jade a doubloon trail into the cavern rather than sulking, and Jade admits she was wrong: it is good to be a little strange. Science-camp logic meets ghost wonder, and the two find their way to the Obsidian Flyer together as believers.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis jumps to the ghost; the script carries the friendship strain (sci camp, the 82%-more-my-friends line), the grounding, Jade's clone worries with Amy, and the doubloon-trail reconciliation in the cavern. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Sam spots a ghost while surfing and tries to convince Jade that something supernatural is going on at Danger Point.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Surfing near Danger Point, Sam wipes out into a hidden cavern and comes up with a gold doubloon and a story Jade refuses to believe, especially now that science camp and its friends are pulling them apart. Grounded and phoneless after paddling out on a red flag, Sam hikes the cliff anyway and leaves a doubloon trail only her best friend would follow. In the cavern, Sam walks through a rock and introduces Jade to Remington Augustus van Roberts, a pirate ghost only believers can see, and Jade the scientist concedes that maybe, possibly, ghosts exist. The fastest galleon in the seven seas awaits.

The overloaded machine backfires spectacularly, the cavern's crystal deposits are revealed as the treasure Pfeiffer hunted, and the festival's ticket sales fund the land surveyor for Danger Point.
stories.coping: The girls bluff the haunted doubloons to scare Olsen into lending his generator, trust each other when the escape looks impossible, and let Devar's grudging help stand as his apology. Remi returns the crystal to its quantum friends in the cavern, Amy's surprise courtyard picnic reunites the family with Dad a day early, and the friends close the summer walking the ghost ship's quarterdeck together.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis compresses the finale; the script carries the doubloon swap and cavern trap, Devar's debt-repaid rescue, the machine backfire that drives Pfeiffer off, the crystals returned to the cavern, Amy's dim-sum courtyard surprise for Dad, the funded land surveyor, and the quarterdeck walk. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Sam and Jade race to stop Dr. Pfeiffer's machine before the Obsidian Flyer vanishes forever, and the Summer Festival saves Danger Point.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The finale stacks the odds: Olsen swaps the girls' doubloons for fakes and strands them in the crystal cavern just as Dr. Pfeiffer powers her machine back up, and only Captain Devar's grudging it is done rescue saves them, his debt repaid. The summer closes the way it opened, with a wipeout's worth of wonder: the Surfside Girls walk the deck of the fastest galleon in the seven seas.

stories.situation: Sam and Jade dig into the vanishing pirate ship with a ghost in tow, touring Old Man Olsen's inaccurate ghost show and discovering Olsen himself capsized near Danger Point years ago and woke in the same glowing cavern. Olsen hands over the antique key he found there and passes the torch, while Petey obsesses over the rival taco truck.
stories.coping: Jade runs the mystery like science: a hypothesis spiral, magnetism from sci camp, and Dr. Pfeiffer's advice to embrace the bizarre and do fieldwork. The friends split leads, compare finds, and agree the untold legend is actually a fraud, which sharpens the real question, what is Olsen's key opening.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the tour only; the script adds Olsen's shipwreck testimony, the key handover, the Dr. Pfeiffer fieldwork advice, the taco-truck rivalry, and the raven-figurehead detail that proves Olsen knows the true story. confidence medium (proposing 'curious' for the vocabulary list; nearest approved terms used).
stories.synopsis: Sam and Jade investigate Danger Point, finding Old Man Olsen's ghost tour and a story about the Obsidian Flyer that doesn't add up.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Sam and Jade take Old Man Olsen's ghost tour of the Obsidian Flyer and Jade fact-checks every word, then confronts him with a doubloon that is real gold. Olsen confesses his own shipwreck long ago: glowing water, a cavern he could never find again, and one antique key he kept ever since. He gives the key to the girls as a passing of the torch, because something strange is going on at Danger Point and the girl with the nagging questions and little Miss Snoopy Pants might get to the bottom of it. Meanwhile Burger Dude braces for the Taco Bruh food truck, and Jade's sci camp advice, embrace the bizarre, becomes the team's method.

stories.coping: Sam risks her mom's disappointment to keep a promise to her friends, and the team works the mystery with cleverness instead of force, cracking the Lady's color code (cat eyes, necklace, feather, gloves) like a puzzle. The near-trap ends with everyone out and a new rule learned: clues need the whole team.

stories.synopsis: A mysterious old film leads Sam and Jade to the Lady of Surfside and her untouched sewing room at the museum.
stories.perStorySynopsis: A museum film called A Weathered Storm shows the very key Old Man Olsen found, and the trail leads to the Lady of Surfside, the museum's vanished founder whose sewing room must stay untouched forever. Sam is stuck at her mom's preservation meeting while Jade and Remi start the heist without her, until Sam chooses her friends and slips out mid-speech. In the forbidden room the girls match a fuchsia cat-eye button, an emerald necklace, and a mustard feather to thread spools, crack a color-code lock, and open a hidden chamber hiding a single queen conch shell. The room nearly buries them, the dumbwaiter saves them, and the shell becomes the newest clue on a board that keeps growing.

The biggest find: the ghost asking for help is the mystery.

At the museum, Mildred's borrowed vintage and a parasol trigger the truth: Remi was a boy rescued from a raided village and carried aboard the Flyer against his mother's cries, and Amy's dad cancels another visit home.
stories.coping: The vision reframes everything Remi thought was abandonment: the Lady's parasol was a gift of smoke-cover protection, not a theft, and Devar's sternness becomes you have someone who will always protect you. stories.situation: Magnetized spires, gray metallic sand, and tire tracks rule out Sam's alien theory and point to an electromagnet machine on wheels, one big enough to shift the earth and explain the erosion. Old Man Olsen has been following them and locks his shed, so the girls stage a stakeout through a brownout-charged night, past their bedtimes, to catch whoever wheels it out.
stories.coping: The friends run the mystery like Jade would want it run, hypothesis first, then evidence, linking brownout times to each piece of the Obsidian Flyer that vanishes six hours later. When the shadowy figure turns out to be someone neither girl expected, Sam has to figure out how to tell Jade a truth she will hate.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis stops at the machine theory; the script carries the tire-track deduction, the committee meeting with Olympia Pfeiffer, the brownout-to-vanishing six-hour pattern, the all-night stakeout past bedtimes, and the cliffhanger reveal that Pfeiffer is the one at Danger Point. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Strange metallic patterns lead Sam and Jade to suspect that a treasure-hunting machine is behind the erosion of Danger Point.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Metallic patterns and magnetized spires at Danger Point spawn Sam's alien theory until tire tracks and iron sand steer the girls toward something man-made: an enormous electromagnet on wheels that could be shifting the earth itself. He stays, mask on, belonging for the first time.

stories.situation: The dream voice promising answers about who Wolfboy really is pulls him sleepwalking toward the forbidden passage, and waking him does nothing. The one entity offering the truth is also the one everyone, including Luxcraft, has barred the door against.
stories.coping: The Dream Lab expedition, raised-by-dreams Oneira and Captain Springhaart, ends at the boundary where the voice wears a face: Nyx, who denies the betrayal story and claims to know what he is truly capable of. Wolfboy declines the new dream, because his dreams might know him better than anyone.
stories.notes: older: sleepwalking, a manipulative stranger in dreams, and refusing a quick fix to keep your own dreams, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'heads to the Dream Lab for help' omits the Nyx contact, the boundary-crossing, and Wolfboy's choice to keep the dream. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: An intense dream causes Wolfboy to sleepwalk toward a forbidden area, so the gang heads to the Dream Lab for help.
stories.perStorySynopsis: A voice in Wolfboy's dreams walks him toward the forbidden passage until his friends chase the sleepwalk through River Lab, then the Dream Lab supplies a new-dream solution and an expedition to the Dreamscape boundary instead. There the voice gains a name, Nyx, who claims the adults are the liars. Wolfboy turns down the replacement dream and keeps his own.

stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Gets a Bed / Wolfboy Makes a Blunder
stories.situation: The rival dorm demands the first-night Star Trial, and refusing means standing out as even more of an outsider than a human pretending to be a spryte already is. The Star Creature hates surface dwellers and Wolfboy cannot float.
stories.coping: He goes anyway, admits the true reason, that a star means he does not have to go home, and the Great Wolf gives him a scale without a trick. Whatever happened at the lake stays a mystery, but he has a bunk and friends who decorated it.
stories.notes: older: high-stakes trial, disguised identity, and a stranger reading the truth, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial' omits the Stargazer confrontation and the honesty payoff. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Sprytes from the rival dorm challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial. Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend.
stories.perStorySynopsis: New kid Wolfboy accepts the rival dorm's Star Trial on his first night rather than be the spryte who refused. At the tower the fearsome Star Creature sees through his disguise, and he wins a star by telling the truth: he just wants to stay. His friends have already made him a bunk.

stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Gets a Bed / Wolfboy Makes a Blunder
stories.situation: In clay class, Wolfboy improvises wings and horns on a rabbit the handbook says must be exact, and Xandra names the result a blunder. Hopton bolts through the factory endangering everyone, headed for a portal to the surface.
stories.coping: The Blunder Dungeon reframes the mistake: a griffin, a wyvern, a jackalope, incredible creatures nobody was supposed to want. Hopton was not rampaging, she needed room to let off steam, and she finds her home with the gamekeeper.
stories.notes: mixed age: the explodeling rabbit chaos plays 2-4; creative work that breaks the rules being called a mistake, and blunders as a home for misfits, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend' omits the handbook conflict, the rampaging sequence, and the Blunder Dungeon reframe. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Sprytes from the rival dorm challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial. Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy's winged explodeling rabbit violates the sacred Spryte Handbook and escapes through the factory, and Xandra calls it what everyone calls wrong creations: a blunder. The Blunder Dungeon shows him a dungeon full of glorious creatures nobody meant to make, and Hopton finds her people. Blunders can be pretty cool.

stories.episodeTitle: There's Trouble in the Wood / Sprout Makes the Team
stories.situation: Flora's wood is fogged and its trees are dying, and the fog hides the cause well enough that no one can fight it. The class stories have also made Sprout terrified that disarrays are everywhere, and getting lost in the fog separates him from the group.
stories.coping: The mystery unpacks in two layers: rotter slugs are the real tree-killers and the fog is their cover, so Wolfboy rebuilds a human contraption with tape and imagination to clear it. The dead tree becomes soil, and Sprout plants it forward.
stories.notes: mixed age: the slug-and-fog mystery plays 2-4; named villains being a cover for a smaller boring problem, and a loss composted into new growth, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'volunteer to care for sick trees' omits the fog cover, the contraption rebuild, and the tree funeral. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout volunteer to care for sick trees. A spryte game between dorms brings out Xandra's competitive side.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Flora's wood is fogged and sick, and the fog turns out to be cover for rotter slugs doing the real damage. Wolfboy rebuilds a human contraption to blow the fog away, the slugs scatter once visible, and one lost tree is buried into the dirt so something new can grow there.

stories.episodeTitle: There's Trouble in the Wood / Sprout Makes the Team
stories.situation: Sprout is the only Figwort left out of Guardians and Disarrays because his dorm cannot field a team, and Xandra knows exactly why joining is risky: they will lose, in public, badly.
stories.coping: Xandra plays anyway for Sprout's sake, hates it, then finds the actual point: they are the worst team and having the most fun. Losing a million games with Sprout beats one point with Tali, and Sprout scores the winning run to a one-sided cheer.
stories.notes: mixed age: the playground game plays 2-4; loyalty versus winning, and choosing the team that lets everyone play, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'brings out Xandra's competitive side' omits Sprout's exclusion, her losing-with-love turnaround, and the win. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout volunteer to care for sick trees. A spryte game between dorms brings out Xandra's competitive side.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Sprout cannot field a Guardians and Disarrays team, so Xandra risks her pride to play on the worst roster in the game. The team loses gloriously and wins anyway, and Xandra's verdict outlasts the score: rather lose a million games with Sprout than win one with the rival dorm.

stories.episodeTitle: Losing Track of Time / Chaos Comes to Class
stories.situation: Wolfboy breaks Sprout's grandfather's twig of enduring friendship, the promise attached to it breaks too, and the apology does not fix the object. The forbidden stairs to the past look like the one undo button.
stories.coping: The trip confirms Chronopher's rule the hard way: touching the past unravels other things, and the stick cannot come home. Sprout breaks the fix-it loop instead, splitting the broken twig into three keepsakes, one for each friend.
stories.notes: older: regret, tampering with the past, and accepting that broken means broken, land 5-7; the keepsake sharing plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake' omits the friendship-token stakes, the near-paradoxes, and the three-ways split resolution. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The gang goes on a time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake. A disarray attack unleashes something really powerful.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy breaks the heirloom twig that sealed his friendship with Sprout, and a stairwell trip to the past teaches the class rule by near-disaster: you cannot unbreak things. Sprout splits the two halves three ways instead, one piece per friend, and the friendship survives its own souvenir.

stories.episodeTitle: Losing Track of Time / Chaos Comes to Class
stories.situation: Guardian Lab's shape-shifting scurillion drills turn real when disarrays infiltrate the training, and friend and foe become indistinguishable on purpose. Wolfboy is the target, and his taped-together gear is dismissed as toys.
stories.coping: Wolfboy learns to read the difference between friends and copies, and Excaliboom, the homemade light lance everyone mocked, is the thing that ends the attack with a boom. The toys were the preparation all along.
stories.notes: older: shape-shifting enemies and trust under pressure land 5-7; the homemade-gadget payoff plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'a disarray attack unleashes something really powerful' omits the scurillion confusion game and the Excaliboom vindication. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: The gang goes on a time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake. A disarray attack unleashes something really powerful.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Guardian Lab's shape-shifter training goes live when disarrays impersonate Xandra, Athena, and friends, and Wolfboy must tell true friends from copies while his homemade gear earns its laughs. Excaliboom's boom ends the attack, and the kid who showed up with toys turns out to be the one who was prepared.

stories.situation: Luxcraft grounds the trio and refuses to say who Wolfboy really is, and the hazy pendant memory is the only thread. Sneaking into a forbidden maze to find your own memories, guarded by memory mites that eat them, is the risk Xandra named a grumpy bum over.
stories.coping: Wolfboy's memory book yields the pendant sighting and a recording of Luxcraft arguing to bring him to the Factory for a destiny someone else is coming for. Xandra's own backstory surfaces, her guardian parents died young, and the three leave the maze closer than they entered it, while the queen's side learns the boy is here.
stories.notes: older: identity mystery, lost parents in a friend's past, and a villain learning where the hero is, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'why Luxcraft's pendant is so familiar' omits the memory mites, the Xandra orphan reveal, and the prophecy argument. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout sneak into the Memory Maze to find out why Luxcraft’s pendant is so familiar to Wolfboy.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Grounded and stonewalled by Luxcraft, Wolfboy sneaks into the Memory Maze to find his own memory of the professor's pendant, with Sprout and a grudging Xandra. The maze answers more than asked: Luxcraft fought to protect a destiny the queen is already hunting, Xandra lost her guardian parents young, and the three friends come out trusting each other with their whole stories.

stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Goes Home / Wolfboy Makes a Snowflake
stories.situation: Wolfboy goes home with a cracked mask and a head full of questions, and every direct one to his mum gets deflected by his own second secret: she thinks he is at a normal school. The attic holds a second wolf mask, younger photos, and a song she used to play him, and still no answer about who he is.
stories.coping: Mum gives him the truest thing she has: nobody can tell you who you are, you figure it out for yourself and listen to your heart. The sprytes' clue hunt turns up a photo that suggests his story is older than either of them has said, and they leave carrying it together.
stories.notes: older: identity questions held open, a parent keeping and receiving secrets, and clues in an attic, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'trip home to see his mother' omits the double secret, the mask mending, and the photo clue. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout join Wolfboy on his trip home to see his mother. Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy brings his spryte friends home to mend Mum-made mask and ask Mum-made questions, all while she believes he is at a human school. The attic yields a twin mask and a photo that deepens the mystery instead of closing it, and his mum hands over the episode's real answer: nobody can tell you who you are, figure it out and listen to your heart.

stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Goes Home / Wolfboy Makes a Snowflake
stories.situation: Blip is a perfectionist about everything except the two things Snow Lab demands: making a unique snowflake and then dancing with it in public. His all-night practicing is already failing before the humiliation part arrives.
stories.coping: Wolfboy hands Blip an ordinary balloon dressed as a dance orb from a rhythm spryte, and the confidence it lends works: Blip dances beautifully. When the reveal comes, the lesson is his to keep, he just had to believe he could do it.
stories.notes: mixed age: the balloon gag plays 2-4; performance anxiety and borrowed confidence becoming real confidence, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence' omits the placebo mechanism and the honest reveal. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout join Wolfboy on his trip home to see his mother. Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Blip can make a perfect snowflake but cannot dance with it in front of anyone, and practice is making him worse. Wolfboy's fake dance orb, actually just a balloon, gives him the belief the night of the performance, and the honest reveal lands gently: the power was Blip's, the orb was a nudge. Snow falls like celebration.

stories.episodeTitle: Grandmother Tells a Story / Grandmother Loses Her Crown
stories.situation: Elderspryte Day at Figwort Farm is a house of caution for a kid whose parents died as heroes: twenty-four siblings, mottoes about running away and curling into a ball, and a family story that ends with the betrayal that lost Xandra her parents. Everyone works hard not to mention them.
stories.coping: Sprout's story fills the gap: Xandra's parents ambushed by scrawmongers and never afraid, told out loud by the kid who never talks about it. The family motto world gets its counterweight, and Xandra lets Wolfboy hold the part of her story nobody says.
stories.notes: older: grieving parents, a family story that names the loss, land 5-7; the farm warmth plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'celebrate Elderspryte Day' omits the motto-of-caution culture, the Great Betrayal story, and Xandra's private story about her parents. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy visits Xandra and Sprout's home to celebrate Elderspryte Day. Grandmother Figwort's beloved crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy spends Elderspryte Day inside the Figworts' loving safety culture, where the mottoes all run away from danger, and learns the reason for Xandra's guardedness: the Great Betrayal story names the day her parents were lost. Her private story about their fearlessness gives the family's caution something to measure up to.
stories.displaySynopsis: Wolfboy spends Elderspryte Day inside the Figworts' loving safety culture, where the mottoes all run away from danger, and learns the reason for Xandra's guardedness: the Great Betrayal story names the day her parents were lost. stories.episodeTitle: Grandmother Tells a Story / Grandmother Loses Her Crown
stories.situation: The bogmarsh beast makes off with Grandmother Figwort's crown, her late husband's one reckless masterpiece of off-path love, and Sprout's whole training is to run away and curl into a ball.
stories.coping: Wolfboy and Xandra lure Sprout off the path to gather new crown flowers, and when the beast returns Sprout stands his ground, scared and offering flowers anyway. His family discovers bravery was a Figwort trait all along, Grandfather Cypress's kind, and the crown is replaced and re-crowned.
stories.notes: mixed age: the beast chase plays 2-4; being scared and doing the thing anyway as a working definition of brave, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast' omits the off-path theme, Grandfather Cypress's story, and Sprout's flower offering. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy visits Xandra and Sprout's home to celebrate Elderspryte Day. Grandmother Figwort's beloved crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The bogmarsh beast steals Grandmother's crown, woven by a late husband who broke every path rule for love, and homebody Sprout must decide which family tradition is his. Off the path, with friends who came to help him be brave, he faces the beast with flowers instead of flight. The new crown earns a hero's badge and a very muddy hug.
stories.displaySynopsis: The bogmarsh beast steals Grandmother's crown, woven by a late husband who broke every path rule for love, and homebody Sprout must decide which family tradition is his. stories.episodeTitle: Nobody Started It! / Wolfboy Begins His Training
stories.situation: The dorm is wrecked, Tali's look convinces everyone who did it, and the retaliation escalates past everyone's intent: glitter dolphins, gravity eggs, water orbs, lights-out citations. Nobody checks the evidence before the first prank flies.
stories.coping: Floof runs the actual investigation: wilted leaves, a rusty spoon, teeth marks, and a disarray identification. The prank war ends with mutual apologies, and the real intruders were after something, or someone.
stories.notes: mixed age: the prank escalation plays 2-4; blame assigned before evidence, and an apology when it was wrong, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'all-out prank war' omits the false accusation of Tali and Floof's disarray forensics. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Dorm rivalry reaches peak silliness with an all-out prank war. Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy to harness his powers.
stories.perStorySynopsis: A trashed dorm room launches a prank war on the rival dorm, built entirely on a look Wolfboy swears was evidence. Floof's actual investigation clears Tali and names the culprit: disarrays, hunting in the dorm for someone. The pranks end in apologies and the mystery gets much bigger.
stories.displaySynopsis: A trashed dorm room launches a prank war on the rival dorm, built entirely on a look Wolfboy swears was evidence. Floof's actual investigation clears Tali and names the culprit: disarrays, hunting in the dorm for someone. The pranks end in apologies and the mystery gets much bigger.

stories.episodeTitle: Nobody Started It! / Wolfboy Begins His Training
stories.situation: Luxcraft confirms the prophecy out loud, a human child who restores balance at a time of great darkness, then locks Wolfboy's questions behind a training contract and a warning: confiding in friends endangers them. Wolfboy's first lie to Xandra and Sprout is already in his mouth.
stories.coping: The wisps get the collaboration not the command: listen, drop the guard, let them see who you really are. The parrot flies, the prophecy is confirmed, and Wolfboy heads back with the secret that will strain his first real friendships.
stories.notes: older: prophecy, secrets kept for other people's safety, and a first lie by omission, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy' omits the prophecy confirmation and the warning that drives his secrecy. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Dorm rivalry reaches peak silliness with an all-out prank war. Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy to harness his powers.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Luxcraft takes Wolfboy to the heart of the Factory to train his wisp-collaboration, and the wisps respond to being seen, not commanded. The prophecy about the human child is confirmed on the record, along with the instruction that keeps it secret even from Sprout and Xandra. Training begins with wonder and a small, growing silence.

stories.episodeTitle: We Laugh and Cry / We Don't Know Who to Trust
stories.situation: Wolfboy is skipping Sprout's play rehearsals for secret world-saving training, telling himself one matters more, and the missed performance ends in detention and a broken stem promise. The apology that would fix it is the one secret he is forbidden to tell.
stories.coping: Wolfboy chooses the friendship over the secrecy and tells the truth: the prophecy, the powers, the wisp cavern, and the danger rule. The friends do not believe him yet, but the breach is honest, and the pipes trip to prove it begins.
stories.notes: older: a broken promise to a friend, the cost of a noble secret, land 5-7; the Laugh Lab play plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment' omits the missed show, the detention, and the full confession. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy's secret training leaves him no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment. Wolfboy tells his friends the truth about the prophecy.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Secret hero training eats every rehearsal for Sprout's Laugh Lab play, and Wolfboy misses the performance itself, detention included. Choosing honesty over the safety rule, he tells his friends about the prophecy and the powers, and they do not believe a word of it, which is its own kind of hurt. The proof trip starts in the pipes.
stories.displaySynopsis: Secret hero training eats every rehearsal for Sprout's Laugh Lab play, and Wolfboy misses the performance itself, detention included. stories.episodeTitle: We Laugh and Cry / We Don't Know Who to Trust
stories.segmentTitle: We Don't Know Who to Trust
stories.situation: The proof expedition through the pipes keeps failing: the Whithervane misleads, Xandra's patience is gone, and a pipe-dweller who lives by never trusting anyone wants the friends to stay broken apart.
stories.coping: The pipe-dweller's birthday-party story shows where distrust leads, living alone in a pipe, and the group chooses each other instead. They reach the wisp cavern in time to overhear the adults deciding what Wolfboy may be allowed to know.
stories.notes: older: trusting a friend who broke a promise, and what never trusting anyone costs, land 5-7; the pipe adventure plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy tells his friends the truth' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy's secret training leaves him no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment. Wolfboy tells his friends the truth about the prophecy.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy leads his doubting friends through the factory pipes to prove the wisp cavern exists, and the journey keeps nearly breaking them, misleading Whithervane and a lonely pipe-dweller teaching distrust. Overhearing Luxcraft and the memory guardians arguing over what Wolfboy should be allowed to know vindicates him: the secret was real, and so was the danger.
stories.displaySynopsis: Wolfboy leads his doubting friends through the factory pipes to prove the wisp cavern exists, and the journey keeps nearly breaking them, misleading Whithervane and a lonely pipe-dweller teaching distrust. stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Takes a Ride / Wolfboy Talks with Nyx
stories.situation: The passage is finally open and Wolfboy walks into the realm everyone fears, alone, on the promise of answers. The spryte side is running a cover story about a sick friend, and Nyx's realm is a wasteland with a two-day wait and generals who do not want him there.
stories.coping: He spends the wait finding a stolen wheel for the disarrays and discovering they are hungry, not evil, which becomes the episode's thesis in one act of seeing them clearly. He reaches Nyx and hears the first version of the truth: the world runs on a cycle of creation and destruction, and both halves matter.
stories.notes: older: crossing into the enemy's world and questioning everything the adults said, land 5-7; the wheel chase plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'steps through the passage and finds the Disarray Realm' omits the humanitis cover story, the stolen wheel, and the balance-of-nature reveal. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy steps through the infamous "passage" and finds himself in the Disarray Realm. Wolfboy finally meets Nyx.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Wolfboy crosses the forbidden passage into the Disarray Realm while his friends stall Luxcraft with a fake case of humanitis. Helping hungry disarrays recover their stolen wheel reframes the enemy, and Nyx's court opens the season's argument: creation and destruction are a cycle, and Wolfboy may be needed by the other side.
stories.displaySynopsis: Wolfboy crosses the forbidden passage into the Disarray Realm while his friends stall Luxcraft with a fake case of humanitis. stories.episodeTitle: Wolfboy Takes a Ride / Wolfboy Talks with Nyx
stories.situation: Nyx tells Wolfboy that the spryte side suppresses destruction, that the twin trees Dryades and Meliae measure the imbalance, and that the prophecy means the disarrays need him. She offers destruction-wisp training and one night to decide.
stories.coping: The episode leaves him mid-persuasion with a disturbingly coherent argument and a court of disarray generals watching. The spryte narrative of good versus evil is complicated for good.
stories.notes: older: moral symmetry, propaganda on both sides, and a mentor with motives, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'finally meets Nyx' omits the Dryades and Meliae balance mechanics and the destruction-wisp offer. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Wolfboy steps through the infamous "passage" and finds himself in the Disarray Realm. Wolfboy finally meets Nyx.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Nyx makes her case: disarrays do necessary work, the twin trees track the world's imbalance, and the prophecy means the disarrays need Wolfboy's help to rise. Destruction-wisp training is on offer, the generals grumble, and the season's central question lands: what if the enemy's story about the world is partly true?
stories.displaySynopsis: Nyx makes her case: disarrays do necessary work, the twin trees track the world's imbalance, and the prophecy means the disarrays need Wolfboy's help to rise. Destruction-wisp training is on offer, the generals grumble, and the season's central question lands: what if the enemy's story about the world is partly true?

stories.situation: Nyx offers to release his friends if he destroys Dryades, the elders accuse him of joining her, and both courts agree on one thing: he is the key. Siding with either means losing someone.
stories.coping: He fakes compliance, then follows the heartbeat to the heart of the factory and destroys both trees to grow one new one: Everyone Portals, usable by sprytes and disarrays alike. The balance is not a side, it is a shared door, and Mum is at the surface end of it.
stories.notes: older: refusing both sides, sacrificing the two trees to build a shared door, land 5-7; the Everyone Portals ending plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'choose between his friends and the fate of the world' omits the fake-out, the heart of the factory, and the Everyone Portals resolution. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Nyx puts Wolfboy in a difficult position, forcing him to choose between his friends and the fate of the world.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Nyx's hostage trade and the elders' accusation leave Wolfboy one move: find the heart of the factory and rebuild from it. Destruction wisps take both old trees, creation wisps grow a new one open to everyone, spryte and disarray, and the prophecy resolves as a door rather than a victory. Wolfboy goes home to tell Mum everything.
stories.displaySynopsis: Nyx's hostage trade and the elders' accusation leave Wolfboy one move: find the heart of the factory and rebuild from it. A shared jargum pellet unlocks real communication, and Eva seals the deal: the grumpy stranger gets the Omnipod to trade in Lacus, and Eva gets a guide to the place her Dynastes patch came from, proof other humans existed. Then Muthr's systems come back online with a harder truth: this world has rings, and it might not be the Earth Eva was raised for.

stories.perStorySynopsis: Season 3 opens inside New Attica with grief turned into war: Eight, told Eva is dead and it is her fault, breaks back in with Vanpa's crew, hacks the city's mainframe, and catches Cadmus in a chase he claims to have scripted all along. Forced to atone on camera, Eight seizes the broadcast instead, showing the citizens the lies behind the dome sky and the truth of the world outside as their birthright. Cadmus's answer closes the trap of the season: he will harness the Source as a weapon and kill every last alien, and he still needs Eight to believe she has no alternative.

stories.situation: Eva survives, reunites with Rovender and Otto, and follows Arius's lead to Queen Ojo in Solas, where Loroc is seizing power by blaming humans for the dying forest. Eva reveals herself to the court, is disbelieved and sentenced, and Zin helps her and the queen escape through a secret exit as Redimus and the loyalists hold the line.
stories.coping: Arius reframes Eva's failure as the future's flexibility, the future is never fixed, and gives her a first step instead of a verdict. Queen Ojo risks her throne to testify that Eva is her friend, and the escape plan is built on trust, the Heart must stay in its casing, and the mission is clear: get to New Attica before Loroc's army does.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the return; the script carries Arius's not-my-sister introduction and ninth-of-Evas naming, the Faunas reunion, the Gargoof-the-shaman disguise gambit, the court reveal, Loroc's coup, Zin's help, the Heart-casing warning, and the thermal-vent plan. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Eva wakes to a dying Orbona, meets the sage Arius, and returns to a Solas on the brink of civil war to find her allies, and herself, on trial.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Eva wakes alone on a dying planet, saves a stranded creature, and finds Arius, Darius's identical sister, who sees all that could be and tells her the future is never fixed. The reunion with Rovender and Otto is brief and warm, and then Eva walks into Solas wearing the face of the enemy's scapegoat: Loroc is using the forest's death to seize his sister's throne. Eva's court reveal gambles everything and nearly loses it, until Zin chooses Orbona over his brother and the queen chooses her friend over her crown. The escape hands the season its quest, deliver the Heart to the thermal vent at the planet's core, with the warning hanging over everything, the Heart must always be in the casing.

stories.situation: A race against pillar guards brings the team to Lacus, where Caruncle has installed himself as viceroy, confiscating fish and heirlooms for Loroc's war and posting a kill-on-sight reward for Eva and the queen. In disguise, Eva and Redimus try to bargain for the Bijou, Redimus is captured, and Hostia shelters the fugitives.
stories.coping: Eva and her friends fight the occupation with nerve and humor, a fake royal-secret-service badge and a boomrod story that riles Caruncle, until the queen takes the boldest path: revealing herself to the city from the Bijou's hatch, calling her people out of the shadows into the light. The crowd cuts the ship loose, Redimus stays to stand with the queen, and a new Omnipod joins the family for the flight to New Attica.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the race; the script carries Vanpa's jargum, the disguise and reward posters, Caruncle's giveaway and viceroy title comedy, Redimus's capture, Hostia's shelter, the queen's hatch speech, the crowd rescue, and the new Omnipod send-off. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: To outrun Loroc's army, Eva and Queen Ojo risk occupied Lacus, face the viceroy who sold it out, and spark a city's rebellion.
stories.perStorySynopsis: Loroc's un-resting pillar guards force a do-or-die detour to Lacus for the Bijou, and the town Eva once visited for a race has fallen: Caruncle the viceroy taxes everything not nailed down, Otto swims in disguise, and a million-shellack bounty hangs over Eva and the queen. The heist for the ship goes sideways when Redimus buys time with his freedom, and Hostia's home becomes the refuge. The rescue is the queen's alone to make: she steps out over the city and asks her people to leave the shadows and fight for their families, and Lacus answers, cutting the Bijou free. The episode ends with Redimus and the queen staying to hold it, and Eva flying on with a chatty new Omnipod and a war to win.

stories.situation: Eva lands near the geothermal vent with the plan set, but Eight, believing Eva died and blaming herself, has seized control of New Attica and orders Eva taken for deprogramming as infected by aliens. When the migrating creatures of Orbona arrive drawn to the Heart, Eight prepares to fire on them, and the sisters stand on opposite sides of the same war.
stories.coping: Eva refuses to fight her sister and instead calls to the herd the way she once talked to Otto, turning the creatures away from the Heart to safety. Rovender tells her never to give up trying to reach Eight, Otto chooses family and promises not goodbye, and Eva admits she does not know if she can restore the Heart, then goes anyway, leading a new band of allies to save Orbona.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the reunion; the script carries the Eight-in-charge reveal and deprogramming order, the Fours resistance and Frank, the migrating herd, the mother-creature shooting and you-are-the-monster line, Eva's herd-turning, and the not-goodbye Otto farewell. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Eva reunites with Eight at last, only to learn that Eight leads New Attica's assault on the aliens, and their reunion becomes a battle over who is the monster.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The reunion Eva crossed a planet for is the season's cruelest twist: Eight survived, leads New Attica now, and greets her sister with a deprogramming cell, convinced Eva has been infected by aliens. Eva's story of the Heart wearing Muthr's face changes nothing, and when Orbona's creatures come migrating home to the Heart, Eight orders weapons free and shoots down a mother. Eva answers with the only power she has, turning the whole herd away from danger with her voice, and walks out of Trievertown with Otto's not-goodbye, a ragtag crew, and a promise she is not sure she can keep: restore the Heart and save Orbona anyway.

stories.situation: Vanpa's repaired warbot smuggles Eva and Redimus into the besieged city, where Eight's forces and the alien army clash as civilians evacuate. The Heart is in Cadmus's office, but Cadmus, freed and chastened, confesses the real horror: Eight weaponized the Source into a bomb atop the pyramid and lured the herd in as a trap.
stories.coping: Eva takes Cadmus at his word and turns an enemy into an ally, if you are sorry, help me. Cadmus gives her the original Omni, universal access and the entire history of their people, and stays behind to face what he built, telling her what Muthr once told her, I will go on and so will you. Otto shields them one last time, saying not goodbye, and Eva presses on toward the thermal vent with Rovender refusing to leave her side.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the search; the script carries Vanpa's warbot infiltration, Redimus's prisoner gambit, the evacuation and battle, the Meego runaway gondola comedy, Cadmus's Project Sunshine confession, the original Omni handoff, and Otto's sacrifice and survival. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: Amid the fog of war, Eva searches New Attica for the Heart, and Cadmus reveals Eight has rigged Project Sunshine, a bomb meant to end every alien on Orbona.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The infiltration of New Attica is part heist, part comedy, and all stakes: Vanpa drives a patched-together warbot, Redimus volunteers as a prisoner, and a Meego-driven gondola nearly ends the quest with french-fry beams. The Heart is found, but so is the season's darkest truth, Eight has turned the Source into Project Sunshine, a bomb luring Orbona's own creatures to their deaths. Cadmus, the villain of two seasons, asks to help fix what he made, hands Eva the original Omni and the history of her people, and stays to hold the line. Otto's not-goodbye and survival carry Eva and Rovender toward the thermal vent with the Heart and almost no time.

stories.situation: Loroc declares himself savior of the planet and blocks the way, Eight confronts Eva as one of them, and Rovender falls in the fighting. At the sealed tunnel, Eva's pleas seem answered only when the very creatures she saved come to her rescue, and Vanpa's Fours buy the last passage with everything they have.
stories.coping: Eva holds the line against becoming what the war wants: she gives Eight jargum so she can finally understand the creatures, and Rovender's last words, do not let this change you, echo Arius's. The Heart answers Eight's returning-home plea with there is no them, only us, Eva names herself the bridge and goes with the Heart, and the epilogue tells the whole arc plainly, a nymph who went in search of a family, a home, and the truth, and found them intertwined.
stories.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis compresses the finale; the script carries Loroc's savior claim and fraud takedown, Vanpa's magnet trap and Evan-4 sign-off, the Fours rescue, Rovender's fall and jargum plea, Eight's seeking-re-entry echo of her own S2 story, Eva going to the Heart as the bridge, and the closing narration with hey, sis. confidence high.
stories.synopsis: With the fate of the planet at stake, Eva races to deliver the Heart to the thermal vent, and Eight must choose between the war she built and the family that never left her.
stories.perStorySynopsis: The finale keeps every promise the series made: Loroc's savior act collapses, Vanpa's magnet trap and the Fours sign-off buy the tunnel, and the creatures Eva once saved come back for her when the way is sealed. Rovender falls, asking only that she not let this change her, and it is Eight, finally given the jargum to hear Orbona speak, who breaks: the Heart greets her the way it once greeted Eva, with there is no them, only us, and the sister who ordered the war chooses re-entry, home, and love. Eva, the bridge, goes with the Heart, and the story ends in narration rather than battle, the world that was become the world that will be, past forgiven, future found, because there is no them, only us.
